scenes.say: Imagine this. You spend over twenty thousand dollars on solar panels.

lines: Then a storm knocks out the power. ⚡
scenes.say: Then a storm knocks out the power.

lines: Next morning, the sun is out.
scenes.say: The next morning, the sun is out. Your panels are sitting in full sunlight.
But your house is still dark.

lines: Most grid-tied solar *shuts off* in a blackout.
scenes.say: Why? Most grid-tied solar systems shut off during a blackout. Even on a sunny day.

lines: ~Your system can't send power onto lines that workers are repairing.
scenes.say: It's a safety rule. Your system can't send power onto lines that workers are repairing.

scenes.kicker: How to keep the lights on:
items: An inverter with a *daytime backup outlet*
scenes.say: So how do you keep the lights on? One: a battery with backup. Two: an inverter with a daytime backup outlet. Three: a generator or a portable power station.

lines: A *10–14 kWh* battery can run your essentials for about *a day*.
scenes.say: A ten to fourteen kilowatt-hour battery can run your essentials for about a day.
